extracted.intended_audience: public water systems, laboratories, State primacy agencies and EPA regulators (and air carriers/operators for the aircraft water system provisions)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements from 40 CFR Part 141 (including aircraft water system provisions and the Revised Total Coliform Rule) describing monitoring, sampling, laboratory, recordkeeping, inspection, corrective action, and reporting obligations for public water systems and aircraft operators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of bacteriological analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must keep records of bacteriological analyses for at least 5 years and must include the following information:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) The date, time, and place of sampling, and the name of the person who collected the sample; (2) Identification of the sample as a routine, repeat, follow-up, or other special purpose sample; (3) Date of the analysis; (4) Laboratory and person responsible for performing the analysis; (5) The analytical technique/method used; and (6) The results of the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of disinfection and flushing
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must keep records of any disinfection and flushing for at least 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must include (1) the date and time of the disinfection and flushing; and (2) the type of disinfection and flushing (i.e., routine or corrective action).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records of self-inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must keep records of a self-inspection for at least 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must include (1) the completion date of the self-inspection; and (2) copies of any written reports, summaries, or communications related to the self-inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain sampling plans and make available for review
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must maintain sampling plans and make such plans available for review by the Administrator upon request, including during compliance audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling plans must be kept current and accessible for regulatory review and audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain aircraft water system O&M plans per FAA
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must maintain aircraft water system operations and maintenance plans in accordance with FAA requirements, and make such plans available for review by the Administrator upon request, including during compliance audits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: O&M plans must conform to FAA requirements and be producible during audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of public notices to passengers and crew
rubrics_metrics.description: The air carrier must keep copies of public notices to passengers and crew issued as required by this subpart for at least 3 years after issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of compliance audits and inspections (aircraft water systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator may conduct routine compliance audits as necessary; compliance audits may include bacteriological sampling, record reviews, and observation of procedures to ensure proper implementation of requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance audits may include: (1) Bacteriological sampling of aircraft water system; (2) Reviews and audits of records as they pertain to water system operations and maintenance such as log entries, disinfection and flushing procedures, and sampling results; and (3) Observation of procedures involving handling of finished water, watering point selection, boarding of water, operation, disinfection and flushing, and general maintenance and self-inspections of aircraft water system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of self-inspection (aircraft)
rubrics_metrics.description: Air carriers or their representatives must perform a self-inspection of all water system components for each aircraft water system no less frequently than once every 5 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely correction of deficiencies (aircraft)
rubrics_metrics.description: Air carrier must address any deficiency identified during compliance audits or routine self-inspections within 90 days of identification, or if identified during extended/heavy maintenance, before the aircraft is put back into service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes any deficiency in design, construction, operation, maintenance, or administration, as well as any failure or malfunction of any system component that has potential to cause unacceptable health risk or affect reliable delivery of safe drinking water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval and operation of supplemental treatment units (aircraft)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any supplemental drinking water treatment units installed onboard existing or new aircraft must be acceptable to FAA and FDA; and must be installed, operated, and maintained in accordance with the manufacturer's plans and specifications and FAA requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental units must be approved by FAA and FDA and installed/operated exactly per manufacturer's and FAA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance of supplemental treatment/production equipment (aircraft)
rubrics_metrics.description: Water supplemental treatment and production equipment must produce water that meets the standards prescribed in this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions constituting violations (aircraft water systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: An air carrier is in violation of this subpart when, for any aircraft water system it owns or operates, specified conditions occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violative conditions include: (a) failure to perform any requirements under §141.803 or §141.804; (b) an E. coli-positive sample in any monitoring period; (c) failure to provide notification to passengers and crew per §141.805; (d) failure to comply with reporting and recordkeeping requirements; (e) failure to conduct a self-inspection or address a deficiency per §141.808; (f) failure to develop a coliform sampling plan per §141.802 or to have and follow an operations and maintenance plan included in an FAA accepted program per §141.804.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart Y applicability, compliance date, and violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart Y (Revised Total Coliform Rule) provisions include MCL and treatment technique requirements and apply to all public water systems; systems must comply beginning April 1, 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems under EPA direct oversight must comply with EPA decisions for implementation; failure to comply with §§141.851–141.861 is a violation of the national primary drinking water regulations under subpart Y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard sample volume for analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard sample volume required for analysis, regardless of analytical method used, is 100 ml.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence/absence testing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems need only determine the presence or absence of total coliforms and E. coli; a determination of density is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for initiation of incubation
rubrics_metrics.description: The time from sample collection to initiation of test medium incubation may not exceed 30 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems are encouraged but not required to hold samples below 10 °C during transit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dechlorination requirement for samples with residual chlorine
rubrics_metrics.description: If water having residual chlorine is to be analyzed, sufficient sodium thiosulfate (Na2S2O3) must be added to the sample bottle before sterilization to neutralize residual chlorine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dechlorination procedures are addressed in Section 9060A.2 of Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater (20th and 21st editions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved analytical methods and versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must conduct total coliform and E. coli analyses in accordance with one of the analytical methods listed in the regulation or one of the alternative methods listed in appendix A to subpart C of part 141.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The methods listed (Standard Methods editions, Standard Methods Online versions, EPA Method 1604, vendor methods, etc.) are the only versions that may be used for compliance. Laboratories should use only the approved versions of the methods, as product package inserts may not be the same as the approved versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory certification for compliance samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must have all compliance samples required under this subpart analyzed by a laboratory certified by the EPA or a primacy State to analyze drinking water samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The laboratory used by the system must be certified for each method (and associated contaminant(s)) used for compliance monitoring analyses under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference and access to referenced materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards required in the analytical methods section are incorporated by reference with approval of the Director of the Federal Register; to enforce any edition other than specified, EPA must publish notice and make material publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved materials are available electronically at regulations.gov, in hard copy at the Water Docket, or from specified sources; copyrighted materials may only be viewed in hard copy; NARA also holds copies. The regulation lists specific referenced documents and vendor method listings (e.g., Standard Methods 20th/21st eds., Standard Methods Online, EPA Method 1604, vendor-specific method documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written sample siting plan requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must develop a written sample siting plan that identifies sampling sites and a sample collection schedule that are representative of water throughout the distribution system not later than March 31, 2016.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These plans are subject to State review and revision. Systems must collect total coliform samples according to the written sample siting plan. Routine and repeat sample sites and any sampling points necessary to meet subpart S must be reflected in the sampling plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of sample collection throughout month
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must collect samples at regular time intervals throughout the month, except that systems using only ground water and serving 4,900 or fewer people may collect all required samples on a single day if they are taken from different sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum sample count regardless of violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must take at least the minimum number of required samples even if the system has had an E. coli MCL violation or has exceeded the coliform treatment technique triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional (optional) compliance monitoring and inclusion rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A system may conduct more compliance monitoring than required to investigate potential problems; additional samples count in trigger calculations only if taken in accordance with the existing sample siting plan and are representative of water throughout the distribution system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat monitoring location requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must identify repeat monitoring locations in the sample siting plan and, unless exceptions apply, must collect at least one repeat sample from the original tap and at least one repeat sample within five service connections upstream and at least one within five service connections downstream of the original sampling site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a total coliform-positive sample is at or one service connection away from the end of the distribution system, the system must still take all required repeat samples. The State may allow alternative sampling locations in lieu of an upstream or downstream repeat. Systems required to conduct triggered source water monitoring must take ground water source sample(s) in addition to repeat samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-approved alternative repeat monitoring locations and SOPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems may propose repeat monitoring locations or criteria (alternative fixed locations or SOP-based selection) to the State if they believe locations represent pathways for contamination; the State may modify or require alternative monitoring locations as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground water systems serving 1,000 or fewer people may propose repeat sampling locations that differentiate potential source water and distribution system contamination (e.g., sampling at entry points). A ground water system with a single well required to conduct triggered source water monitoring may, with written State approval, take one repeat sample at the triggered source water monitoring location if the sample siting plan remains representative. Specific rules apply for counting E. coli-positive repeat samples vis-à-vis MCL and §141.402 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: State review/approval of repeat sampling and representativeness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: States may review, revise, and approve repeat sampling proposed by systems; the system must demonstrate that the sample siting plan remains representative of the distribution system water quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State may determine monitoring at the entry point to the distribution system is effective to differentiate between potential source water and distribution system problems, particularly for undisinfected ground water systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special purpose sample exclusion from trigger calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Special purpose samples (e.g., taken to determine sufficiency of disinfection following pipe work) must not be used to determine whether the coliform treatment technique trigger has been exceeded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat samples taken pursuant to §141.858 are not special purpose samples and must be used to determine whether the treatment technique trigger has been exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and documentation for invalidation of total coliform-positive samples by State
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may invalidate a total coliform-positive sample only if one of specified conditions is met: (i) lab establishes improper analysis caused the result; (ii) State determines, based on repeat sample results, that the positive resulted from domestic or other non-distribution plumbing problem (with constraints); or (iii) State has substantial grounds to believe the result is due to a circumstance not reflecting distribution system water quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To invalidate under (iii) the system must still collect all required repeat samples; the decision and supporting rationale must be documented in writing, approved and signed by the supervisor of the recommending State official, made available to EPA and the public, state the specific cause, and state corrective actions. The State may not invalidate solely because all repeat samples are total coliform-negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory invalidation requirements for interference and required follow-up sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: A laboratory must invalidate a total coliform sample (unless total coliforms are detected) if the sample produces a turbid culture without gas formation where gas formation is examined, produces a turbid culture in absence of an acid reaction in the P-A test, or exhibits confluent growth or colonies too numerous to count with membrane filter methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a laboratory invalidates a sample because of such interference, the system must collect another sample from the same location within 24 hours of being notified and have it analyzed for total coliforms, and continue re-sampling every 24 hours until a valid result is obtained. The State may waive the 24-hour time limit on a case-by-case basis or implement criteria for waiving the time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine monitoring and follow-up after a total coliform-positive (small non-community GW systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-community water systems using only ground water and serving 1,000 or fewer people, following any total coliform-positive sample systems must comply with repeat monitoring requirements and E. coli analytical requirements in §141.858.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once monthly monitoring is complete, systems must determine whether any coliform treatment technique triggers in §141.859 have been exceeded and complete assessments if triggers exceeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring frequency and transition rules (small non-community GW systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must monitor each calendar quarter the system provides water to the public, except for seasonal systems or as otherwise provided; systems on prior §141.21 schedules continue unless increased monitoring triggers or State direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginning April 1, 2016 the State must perform a special monitoring evaluation during each sanitary survey to review the system's status and monitoring schedule; State may modify monitoring schedule only consistent with section criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual site visit / Level 2 assessment requirement for annual monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning no later than calendar year 2017, systems on annual monitoring must have an initial and recurring annual site visit by the State equivalent to a Level 2 assessment or an annual voluntary Level 2 assessment that meets criteria in §141.859(b) to remain on annual monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A periodic required sanitary survey may be used to meet the annual site visit requirement for the year the sanitary survey was completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for eligibility for annual monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may reduce monitoring frequency from quarterly to annual for a well-operated ground water system if the system demonstrates: (1) a clean compliance history for a minimum of 12 months; (2) the most recent sanitary survey shows the system is free of sanitary defects or has corrected all identified sanitary defects, has a protected water source, and meets approved construction standards; and (3) the State has conducted an annual site visit within the last 12 months and the system has corrected all identified sanitary defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Level 2 assessment that meets §141.859(b) criteria may substitute for the State annual site visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggers requiring increased monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: A system on quarterly or annual monitoring that experiences any of specified events must begin monthly monitoring the month following the event (or quarterly for some annual-monitoring triggers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers include: (1) system triggers a Level 2 assessment or two Level 1 assessments in a rolling 12-month period; (2) the system has an E. coli MCL violation; (3) the system has a coliform treatment technique violation; (4) system has two subpart Y monitoring violations or one subpart Y monitoring violation and one Level 1 assessment in a rolling 12-month period (for systems on quarterly monitoring); (5) the system has one subpart Y monitoring violation for a system on annual monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to return to quarterly monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The State may reduce a system on monthly monitoring (triggered under increased monitoring rules) back to quarterly monitoring if the system meets specified criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria: (1) within last 12 months the system must have a completed sanitary survey or a site visit by the State or voluntary Level 2 assessment approved by the State, be free of sanitary defects, and have a protected water source; and (2) the system must have a clean compliance history for a minimum of 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to qualify for annual monitoring after increased monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: A system on increased monitoring may be reduced to annual monitoring only if it meets the criteria to return to quarterly monitoring and additional annual-monitoring criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional criteria: (1) an annual site visit by the State and correction of all identified sanitary defects (or substitute voluntary Level 2 assessment by a State-approved party); and (2) the system must have in place or adopt one or more additional enhancements to water system barriers to contamination, such as: (i) cross connection control approved by the State; (ii) an operator certified by an appropriate State certification program or regular visits by a certified circuit rider; (iii) continuous disinfection entering the distribution system and a residual in the distribution system per State criteria; (iv) demonstration of maintenance of at least a 4-log removal or inactivation of viruses as provided under §141.403(b)(3); or (v) other equivalent enhancements as approved by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonal system start-up and monitoring rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning April 1, 2016, seasonal systems must demonstrate completion of a State-approved start-up procedure (which may include startup sampling) and must monitor every month they are in operation unless they meet criteria for less frequent monitoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seasonal systems monitoring less frequently than monthly must have an approved sample siting plan that designates the time period(s) for monitoring based on site-specific considerations (e.g., during highest demand/vulnerability); to be eligible for quarterly or annual monitoring they must meet the criteria in (g) or (h) respectively. The State may exempt seasonal systems from some requirements if the entire distribution system remains pressurized during the entire non-operation period, except systems that monitor less frequently than monthly must still monitor during the vulnerable period designated by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional routine monitoring following a total coliform-positive (quarterly/annual systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems collecting samples on a quarterly or annual frequency must conduct additional routine monitoring the month following one or more total coliform-positive samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must collect at least three routine samples during the next month (State may waive in certain conditions). Samples may be collected at regular intervals throughout the month or on a single day if taken from different sites. Results of additional routine samples must be used in coliform treatment technique trigger calculations under §141.859(a). The State may waive the three-sample requirement if the State or an approved agent performs a sufficiently detailed site visit before the end of the next month in which the system provides water to the public.
